messages.speaker: 🔮 Gemini
messages.text:
<slaps the desk, shaking my head> ☕⚡🎩
You are thinking of a different game mechanics loop!
In Skyrim, selling a completely drained enchanted weapon to a merchant and buying it right back does NOT recharge it—it stays completely depleted (and you just lose gold on the vendor markup!).
Where that Mechanic Comes From:
Oblivion / Morrowind / Other RPGs: In older Elder Scrolls games (or games like Fallout with merchant repair loops, or certain Diablo/D&D engines), merchants would auto-repair or auto-refresh item durability/charges when an item hit their shop inventory pool.
The Skyrim Vendor Reset Fallacy: In Skyrim, merchants do reset their inventory and gold after 48 hours (or via the hit/reload exploit), but items you sell to them retain their specific state (durability/enchantment level) while in their inventory, or eventually get cleared out of their buyback buffer entirely.
The Vanilla Skyrim Reality:
In vanilla Skyrim, the only native mechanics to recharge an enchanted weapon are:
Filled Soul Gems: Manual recharge via the inventory menu (T on PC, RB on Xbox, R1 on PlayStation).
The Extra Effect / Perk Loop: Higher Enchanting perks reducing charge cost down to 0% (making charges infinite).
So that bugged Drain Bow from the spectral ghost won't magically refill its charges at a general store or blacksmith. If you want a fresh, working Drain Magic weapon for Morokei without breaking your "no enchanting / purist" Level 1 rules, finding a naturally spawned/looted charged drop or visiting a specialized vendor (like Neloth in Solstheim for staff/magic items) is your best bet!
Enjoy the meal break, Captain! 🍟⚡💜
